positions.subject: q:housing/citywide-rezoning
positions.summary: In GrowSF's questionnaire his answer called Mayor Lurie's Family Zoning plan a step in the right direction but not ambitious enough by itself, and said future housing growth must be shared across every San Francisco neighborhood.

citations.quote: Mayor Lurie’s Family Zoning plan is a step in the right direction, but by itself it is not ambitious enough to solve San Francisco’s housing challenges.
citations.locator: Housing: "Do you think Mayor Lurie’s Family zoning plan is too ambitious or not ambitious enough?"

citations.quote: District 10 has carried more than its fair share of new development over the years, so future housing growth must be equitable across every neighborhood in San Francisco.
citations.locator: Housing: "Do you think Mayor Lurie’s Family zoning plan is too ambitious or not ambitious enough?"

positions.subject: q:public-health/end-drug-use-supply-distribution
positions.summary: In GrowSF's questionnaire, said he would keep syringe access and naloxone distribution but change course on blanket or poorly monitored distribution of pipes and foil: audit those programs on outcomes and reduce unmanaged public distribution in favor of supervised or structured settings.

citations.quote: I would not approach this as an all-or-nothing issue.
citations.locator: answer to "Would you continue or change the city’s harm reduction policies that distribute drug use paraphernalia beyond clean needles, such as pipes, foil, etc.?" (Substance Abuse section)

citations.quote: Where I would change course is around the broader expansion of paraphernalia distribution, such as pipes and foil, when it is done in a blanket or poorly monitored way.
citations.locator: answer to "Would you continue or change the city’s harm reduction policies that distribute drug use paraphernalia beyond clean needles, such as pipes, foil, etc.?" (Substance Abuse section)

citations.quote: Reduce unmanaged public distribution if it is contributing to sidewalk use or environmental impacts, and instead concentrate services in supervised or structured settings.
citations.locator: answer to "Would you continue or change the city’s harm reduction policies that distribute drug use paraphernalia beyond clean needles, such as pipes, foil, etc.?" (Substance Abuse section)
